ai.title: turnspendlimit 429 stops SDK retries, shows server copy
ai.summary: SDK model-provider now throws non-retryable APICallError on 429 with error code turn_spend_limit. AI SDK previously retried 4x over ~14s, misframing the error as a generic rate limit. CLI error-handling and common constants updated to surface the breaker's specific message instead of a retry countdown. Covers SDK, CLI, and shared error definitions.

eli5.text: When you send a message that uses up too much of your turn's usage budget, the assistant now stops trying to retry the request and instead shows you a clear message explaining that something went wrong with that turn. This only affects you if you hit that per-turn spending limit (a 429 error with code 'turn_spend_limit'), previously the system would retry four times over about fourteen seconds and then fail with a generic 'too many requests' message that looked like an ordinary rate limit. Now, hitting that specific limit immediately shows the server's explanation and tells you to send a new message to continue, rather than making you wait through retries that don't work. This is live today across the CLI, shared error definitions, and the SDK model-provider.

facts: Whether the demand attached third-party measurement, and in which channel. Without this we cannot tell "the partner sent no trackers" from "we dropped them", which is exactly the question that gets asked when an advertiser reports missing impressions.
Third-party measurement attached by the demand partners funding an Imprezia ad, delivered from the end user's device.

Delivering it is not optional. These pixels and frames belong to the advertiser's own measurement vendor, not to Imprezia: an ad whose trackers never fire is one the advertiser never counts as delivered, however correctly we report it on our own beacon.
This has to run on the END USER'S device. Firing these server-side would carry a datacenter IP and a server UA and be discounted as invalid traffic, which is the same as not delivering them at all.
Hygiene on a long-lived page: drop the frame once it has loaded.

ai.title: Gravity user agent resolution uses real client header
ai.summary: Added `resolveGravityUserAgent` to serve the real client user agent to Gravity instead of forcing browser-like UAs. Gravity requested the actual client (e.g. `Codebuff-CLI/<v>`) on 2026-09-04 because ~74% of traffic was misreported as Chrome desktop. The function prefers the trimmed `requestHeader`, falling back to the browser-like UA if missing or blank. Scope: `common/src/util/ad-user-agent.ts`.

eli5.text: Starting today, when the system sends information to its advertising partner called Gravity, it now passes along the real browser or app details from your device instead of pretending you are using a regular web browser. If your device did not send those details, it falls back to the generic browser information so nothing breaks. This fixes a problem where roughly three-quarters of traffic was being incorrectly reported as regular Chrome desktop users. You would notice the difference only if you were checking the advertising reports, where the traffic now shows up with its true source.

ai.summary: MUSE_SPARK_FALLBACK_AFTER_MS raised from 10_000 to 15_000 in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts. The increase compensates for the new key pool logic in web/src/llm-api/meta-key-pool.ts, where rate-limited requests now iterate through independent per-team buckets before waiting. This extends the patience window for cases where all keys are exhausted, preventing premature model fallback while leveraging faster resolution via pool rotation.

eli5.text: The assistant now waits a little longer, 15 seconds instead of 10, before giving up when it can't reach the model and decides to switch to a backup plan. This mainly affects you when lots of people are hitting the model at once and every key to get in is temporarily blocked. With the new key-pool system, the assistant now automatically tries another available key behind the scenes before waiting, so the longer window is only the final fallback when nothing works. If you looked, you'd notice a slightly longer pause before the model switches rather than an immediate switch on a busy moment.

ai.title: Plan mode toolset enforcement
ai.summary: Plan mode now enforces restrictions via the toolset, not just prompt prose. `str_replace`, `write_file`, `basher`, `tmux-cli`, and editor agents are withheld when `planOnly` is true. This prevents accidental file edits and commits during planning turns. The worked example in the prompt also branches to show plan-only behavior.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to think through a plan instead of building right away (Plan mode), it can no longer make edits, run commands, write to your files, or commit anything during that turn, it only delivers the written plan in <PLAN> tags and tells you to switch out of Plan mode to have it built. The restriction now lives in the assistant's available tools rather than just in the prompt, closing the gap that previously let a Plan turn silently build and commit a whole feature. This affects anyone using Plan mode starting today.
